question: The number of valence electrons in a group _________ when we are moving down.
solution:
The correct answer is __**remains constant**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Valence electrons** are the outermost electrons of an atom and are crucial for determining how the atom interacts with other atoms.
 
• In a group of the periodic table, the number of valence electrons **remains constant** as you move down from one element to the next.
 
• This is because elements in the same group have similar chemical properties and the same number of electrons in their outermost shell.
 
• For example, all elements in **Group 1 (alkali metals)** have one valence electron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The periodic table is arranged in such a way that elements with similar properties fall into the same vertical columns, known as groups.
 
• While the number of valence electrons remains constant within a group, the number of electron shells increases as you move down the group, leading to larger atomic radii.
 
• This constancy in the number of valence electrons is a key reason why elements in the same group exhibit similar chemical behavior.
 
• Understanding the behavior of valence electrons is essential for predicting the chemical reactivity and bonding characteristics of elements.
